headline: South Asia: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government.
- Western Russia: Three killed and four injured in Russian strike on critical infrastructure facility in Dnipro.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran unveils massive underground 'missile city' as IRGC warns of violent global response.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Merl Grove teachers revolt over principal’s leadership style.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 16 hours ago: Merl Grove teachers revolt over principal’s leadership style.
Merl Grove High School Chairman David Hall is warning that prolonged tensions at the St Andrew institution could undermine students’ success, as he calls on the Ministry of Education to urgently intervene following Monday’s teachers’ protest over the leadership of Principal Dr Marjorie Fullerton. “It is urgent, and we want the best for our girls, ... but we cannot get the best if the teacher staff is not happy,” Hall told The Gleaner.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 16 hours ago: Jamaica too blessed not to be a developed country, says TEF boss.
WESTERN BUREAU: The potential earnings from Jamaica’s tourism sector by 2036 must translate into wealth for all Jamaicans, not just those directly involved in the sector, says Dr Carey Wallace, executive director of the Tourism Enhancement Fund (TEF). Speaking with The Gleaner on Saturday during the Rondel Village Resort and Spa’s 40th anniversary celebration in Negril, Westmoreland, Wallace said that the Ministry of Tourism’s ongoing Tourism 3.0 programme is geared toward building wealth across all of Jamaica’s industries.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Malvinas: Argentina asks Law of the Sea tribunal to halt UK oil exploration.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 5 hours ago: Malvinas: Argentina asks Law of the Sea tribunal to halt UK oil exploration.
The Argentine delegation presented its case in Hamburg, warning that oil extraction in an area subject to a sovereignty dispute would cause irreversible damage La entrada Malvinas: Argentina asks Law of the Sea tribunal to halt UK oil exploration se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Three killed and four injured in Russian strike on critical infrastructure facility in Dnipro.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Three killed and four injured in Russian strike on critical infrastructure facility in Dnipro.
Russian forces have attacked a critical infrastructure facility in Dnipro, killing three people and injuring at least four others.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Recent Ukrainian strikes have reduced Russian oil processing capacity by 30%, says Reuters.
Renewed drone attacks on major Russian refineries have disrupted operations at nine key facilities, reducing domestic crude processing capacity by roughly 30%.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Zelenskyy reveals contents of €643m aid package from Denmark.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Denmark's new military aid package, worth roughly €643 million, will fund purchases of attack drones, interceptor drones, and ammunition for F-16 fighter jets. Part of the package will go towards the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), a US-NATO programme that enables NATO allies to purchase US-made weapons for Ukraine.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian FPV drones attack municipal workers twice in Kramatorsk, killing two and injuring one.
Russian FPV drones struck a refuse collection vehicle on 10 November, killing a worker and seriously injuring another. A similar attack killed a colleague the previous day.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Poland says Pentagon backs permanent US base, with Trump decision due in December.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Poland says Pentagon backs permanent US base, with Trump decision due in December.
Warsaw is seeking a lasting American military commitment as NATO allies fear further U.S. troop withdrawals from Europe.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: UN Court Rejects Bosnian Serb War Criminal’s Early Release Plea Again.
The court said former Bosnian Serb interior minister Mico Stanisic, who is serving 22 years in prison for war crimes, has failed to "sufficiently demonstrate rehabilitation".
- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Turkey Bans Media Reporting on Deadly Factory Blast in Izmir.
Authorities ban media from reporting deadly factory blast in Izmir province that has killed 17 workers, prompting concerns over public's right to access information.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran unveils massive underground 'missile city' as IRGC warns of violent global response.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Iran unveils massive underground 'missile city' as IRGC warns of violent global response.
IRGC Maj.-Gen. Abdollahi warned of retaliation beyond the Middle East if Iran faced renewed attacks. “If the enemy makes another move against us, our response will extend beyond the region,” he said.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Israeli president warns against repeat election in new Knesset session.
Herzog calls for an inquiry into the October 7 attacks during a Knesset session amid political gridlock following elections.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: Israel to expand Iron Beam integration as laser system set for bigger role in warfare by year's end.
Israel is far more ready now for the Hezbollah FPV drone threat than it was in early 2026, but there is still a learning curve, the Post has learned.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Iran backs nuclear treaty even as hardliners raise prospect of bomb.
Iran says it is committed to non-proliferation treaty, but hardliners may be pushing for a change in nuclear policy.
Africa - bottom line: DRC: FRN intensifies offensive, putting FARDC under pressure on multiple fronts.
- Africanews, 6 hours ago: DRC: FRN intensifies offensive, putting FARDC under pressure on multiple fronts.
Security is once again deteriorating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. In South Kivu, clashes between Congolese forces, backed by Wazalendo militia, and FRN fighters, formerly known as AFC/M23, are intensifying across several front lines.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 16 hours ago: Nigeria: Troops Eliminate 58 Terrorists Across Nigeria, Arrest 92 Criminals in One Week.
[This Day] Abuja -- The Nigerian Military said troops deployed to different theatres of operation across the federation successfully repelled terrorist attacks and eliminated more than 58 terrorist fighters.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: East Africa: Cross-Border Chaos - How Are War Economies Threatening the Countries of the Horn of Africa?.
[Nile Post] For decades, countries across the Horn of Africa have faced persistent threats driven by war economies, particularly as Somalia and Sudan have descended into cycles of conflict and internal fighting, alongside the growing influence of terrorist organisations. These developments, in turn, have affected neighbouring countries, as is evident along the Sudanese-Ethiopian border, where a scheme is reportedly being carried out to forcibly recruit young people from Tigray to fight in Sudan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 17 hours ago: Nigeria: Turkiye - Nigeria Deploying Turkish Drones, Helicopters in Anti-Terror Operations - Envoy.
[Daily Trust] Turkish-supplied attack helicopters and uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become critical operational assets for the Nigerian Armed Forces in counter-terrorism operations, the Turkish Ambassador to Nigeria, Mehmet Poroy, revealed during a press conference in Abuja.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: South Africa: Nine in Court for Alleged Contravention of Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act 15 of 1998.
[SAnews.gov.za] Nine foreign nationals have appeared in two separate courts in Gauteng, following their arrest in connection with an alleged attempt to travel from South Africa to participate in the Russia-Ukraine war.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: South Africa: Angry MK Party Volunteers Tell Zuma No Council Seats for Election Flops.
[Scrolla] The Nxamalala Detachment claims provincial leaders have put themselves forward for council seats despite failing to deliver good election results. The group's chairperson confirmed the letter was intended for party leaders but declined to discuss the grievances while awaiting Zuma's response.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Malawi: Lawyer Soko Sounds Alarm Over Malawi's Jobs Crisis As Graduates Queue for Work.
[Nyasa Times] Private practice lawyer Khumbo Soko has raised the alarm over Malawi's jobs crisis, warning that graduates are sitting at home while the country spends scarce resources training them.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Malawi: Roads Authority Digs in Over K587bn Road Contracts After HRDC Challenge.
[Nyasa Times] The Roads Authority has mounted a robust defence of its decision to award K587.12 billion in contracts for the rehabilitation of the Chiweta-Karonga section of the M1, rejecting suggestions of impropriety and insisting the procurement process was both competitive and compliant with established rules.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government.
Israel’s parliament was sworn in on Tuesday without a new government, after a deadlocked general election stripped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power. Lawmakers elected in the Oct 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot, a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel’s president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government. Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment effort as 'farce'.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading multiple military operations that have sparked allegations of misconduct against the Pentagon chief. Under pressure after President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections, Hegseth now faces a congressional effort to remove him from office.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Africanews, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, The Moscow Times, 2 hours ago: US calls for new Europe security framework as Russia, Ukraine hold first peace talks in 9 months.
A first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended on Tuesday, with Washington calling for a “new” security framework, as Europe fears US President Donald Trump plans a deal with Moscow on the continent’s future. Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff brought together the warring sides for several hours of negotiations — the first since February — that are set to continue on Wednesday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Britain says its bases are safe after US refuelling planes evacuated.
Britain said on Tuesday that its military bases were safe, after the US removed huge refuelling aircraft from a British airbase following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran, the second such apparent evacuation in three months. Commercially available flight tracking data showed at least 10 Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker refuelling planes left the Royal Air Force base in Mildenhall, eastern England, on Monday. One flew to a base in Germany, one to Scotland and two to Spain, while the destinations of the other six were not reported.
Asia - bottom line: US’ Hegseth calls impeachment bid a ‘farce’ as he defends Iran war.
- South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: US’ Hegseth calls impeachment bid a ‘farce’ as he defends Iran war.
US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth called an impeachment bill against him a “farce” on Tuesday, defending the ongoing war in Iran and the air strikes against drug traffickers as “lawful operation”. - South China Morning Post - China, 12 hours ago: Could US Marines sustain a war with China? Officers warn of Pacific weaknesses.
US Marines deployed across the western Pacific could struggle to sustain their forces, move missile batteries and secure permission to launch operations from allied territory in a conflict with China, according to assessments by Marine Corps officers and independent analysts. - South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: After fridge hacks, home appliances could be next, EU cyber chief warns.
After recent attacks on supermarket fridges, home appliances could be next, the EU’s cyber chief said on Tuesday, as he urged Europe to invest more to counter growing cyber threats. Supermarkets in at least 12 European countries were hit by cyberattacks in October and November, with France the worst affected. “Security should not and cannot be an afterthought,” Juhan Lepassaar, executive director of the EU’s cybersecurity agency ENISA, said. “Today it was fridges, tomorrow it could be routers,...
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: China hands over remains of US airmen killed during World War II supply missions.
China has handed over the remains of American airmen who were killed during World War II while carrying supplies over the Himalayas. The Chinese and US militaries held a handover ceremony in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan province, on Tuesday to transfer remains excavated from sites along “the Hump”, a treacherous airlift route between India and China. - Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: 'Almost all of Iran's oil revenue will dry up': Rubio warns as US tightens sanctions.
US secretary of state Marco Rubio warned that Iran could face devastating losses in oil revenue due to upcoming sanctions. He mentioned that the US treasury department is actively seeking to disrupt Iran's strategies to evade these sanctions. Diplomatic ties between the two nations appear frozen, with each side holding firm to conflicting negotiation terms.
- NDTV - Top Stories, just now: "Everything We Love Is At Stake": Greta Thunberg Arrives For COP31 Summit.
The COP31 conference is being held in the Turkish resort city of Antalya following a year of deadly climate-related disasters, including heat waves and floods, and another energy shock caused by the Iran war.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Texas family wins $21.6m after sewer vents found ending in home's attic.
A Texas family has been awarded more than $21.6 million after faulty plumbing sent sewer gas into their home, which they bought in 2018. A plumber later found that the sewer vents ended in the attic. The family reported health problems and had to leave the house, which remains uninhabitable.

- NK News, 14 hours ago: North Korean leader’s sister slams UN chief over DMZ mine blast remarks.
The North Korean leader’s sister Kim Yo Jong accused the U.N. secretary-general of taking a “prejudiced and irresponsible attitude” toward tensions on the Korean Peninsula on Tuesday, after he recently warned of escalation risks along the inter-Korean border. Australia - bottom line: You’ll hear the usual cliches about war this Remembrance Day – why does Australia refuse to learn the true lessons of history? | Paul Daley.
- The Guardian - Australia, 8 hours ago: You’ll hear the usual cliches about war this Remembrance Day – why does Australia refuse to learn the true lessons of history? | Paul Daley.
Our national identity is becoming increasingly militarised. Today I’m thinking of a mother’s words – not the veneration of war dished out by politicians Countless are the times politicians have spoken for the Australian military personnel whose names appear on the roll of honour at the Australian War Memorial because they were killed in service. Three men are charged by US authorities with plotting a "campaign of terror" of nearly 20 attacks targeting Jewish communities in Europe and the US and the British military base at RAF Fairford.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: 100yo soldier gets medals recognising service eight decades on.
Ian Hart wore replica medals for decades after serving in the Australian Army. He has now been awarded the official service medals he earned.

A motorcycle rider and a car driver died at the scene after their vehicles collided, with police investigating the circumstances.
